summary: Sound stage-3 design that targets the measured A8 bottleneck (2x stage-1's per-byte time, throughput-bound at the 128-reg cap) with a warpgroup-per-kv-head wgmma mapping that fits the M=64 shape exactly; proceed as an okc check, fixing the fallback to restore master's PAIRED FA3 path (not the unpaired one) and bounding every mbarrier wait so a protocol bug fails fast instead of hanging to the 15-minute timeout.
justification: A: The mechanism is plausible on H100. Each kv head's 8 q heads x 8 block tokens form exactly one wgmma M=64 tile. QK is 2 x m64n64k32 e4m3 per 64-token tile and PV is 2 more, so tensor-core work is negligible. Softmax is about 8K exp2 per 16 KB tile per CTA. At 2 CTA/SM that is roughly 40% of MUFU throughput at a ~3 TB/s gather rate, so the math can hide under the gather once the per-tile __syncthreads and cooperative f16 V-widen are gone. FA3 itself does this verify at ~2.0-2.2 TB/s (150.7 us main at verify_16). REWRITE_READ section 2 supports the diagnosis: A8 scales linearly with bytes (447.7/227.8 = 1.97x), at 1.45 TB/s against stage-1 decode A's 2.94 TB/s on the same gather machinery, at exactly 128 regs. That points to a per-tile throughput limit, not tail or latency. Register budget: S 32 + O 32 + P 8 + row stats + addresses comes to about 100 regs, under the 128 cap. Smem: stage 2's 90.6 KB + 16 KB Vt + 1024-B swizzle alignment comes to about 108 KB/CTA, which still allows 2 CTA/SM within 228 KB, but only just; print the occupancy. The expected directions match TASK.md: only full verify_16/32 (weight 16 each) are gated, every other shape keeps master, and the milestone numbers (incumbent 162.7/301.3, floors 63.4/126.8) match the read. The in-kernel ticket combine replaces B8 (13.9-17.8 us, about 2x FA3 combine+norm-gate) with a B-way parallel LSE merge of about grid/B slots x 32 KB per request at the tail. That costs an estimated 2-4 us and removes a launch, so it is a credible additional ~10 us. WEAKEST LINK: the cause of A8's 2x slowdown is inferred ('likely serializers'), not measured. Nothing was stamped per phase, and stage 2 sat at the register cap, so the wgmma restructure could hit a different limit: the fp8 C->A prmt, the per-warpgroup V transpose (32-bit loads + prmt + stores + named barrier on every tile), or mbarrier latency with only 4 stages. Even a perfect M2 (main kernel <= 1.15x stage-1 decode A) leaves verify at ~1.9-2.0x floor, so M3 (<= 1.5x floor, ~3.2 TB/s) needs a gather rate stage 1 never reached and is out of this stage's reach. That limits the stage, but it does not argue against running it. Secondary design risks: (1) the ring must store each stage's K rows contiguously at a 128-B pitch (separate K and V sub-buffers, SBO 1024 B per 8-row group) for the SW128 K-major B descriptor to be valid; if the stage-2 per-token layout interleaves K and V (256-B pitch), the descriptor and swizzle math must change. (2) Advancing the start address by 32*kstep + 64*g bytes inside a 128B-swizzle atom is legal (CUTLASS does it), but the Q A-operand uses a different swizzle (64B), so the two descriptors must be built independently.
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (stage 1, landed): the stage-3 kernel reuses its gather and page-prefetch machinery but builds in a separate module, so decode must stay byte-identical on master's muse_full_decode_splitkv_v1. Rebasing the stage-2 branch (which renamed and extended that module to v2 with A8/B8) must not carry v2's decode changes over. If B8 is kept as the ticket fallback, it has to be compiled into the new wgmma module, not into master's decode module. Full decode_32 drifts up to 6% between runs with identical kernels (LESSONS), so any headline movement there is noise; stage 2's '1.14x on decode_32' was already ruled a scoring artifact.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing + paired-heads-launch-cleanup (+ ab-tune-batch-gate): master runs full verify_16/32 on the PAIRED FA3 path. The stage-3 gate turns pairing off for those shapes, so _pre_attention_kernel switches to the unpaired q layout there (a small, real time change at 2-4 us, included in the shape's time but not in the 'replaced' set). More importantly, the spec's fallback says 'master (unpaired FA3 path)'. Master is the paired path. An unpaired-FA3 fallback would be slower than master (pairing gained ~1.17x), so a fallback run would read as a regression attributable to nothing in the kernel. The fallback must clear the verify gate so that paired = window == 0 and hkv % 2 == 0 and batch > 1 and not splitkv and not splitkv_verify evaluates True again.

fused-preattention-triton: it supplies the FP8 q that becomes the wgmma A operand (unpaired layout [B*8, 16, 64]). The Q-block smem load must match that layout exactly; it does not change the measurement otherwise.

sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv / sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: different shapes, no interaction beyond import-time build cost (a third load_inline module adds ~45 s+ of the 15-minute budget).
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite stage judged on the replaced kernels' own profile time (splitkv_verify_wgmma_kernel, plus B8 if the ticket falls back) against the incumbent's 162.7/301.3 us and floors of 63.4/126.8 us. That reading does not depend on the headline, so neither a gain nor a loss is ambiguous in a way an extra run would resolve. An ab-revert of the pairing hypotheses would only change the fallback path, which is not what is being measured. A control isolating the ticket combine from the wgmma compute is unnecessary: the profile shows whether B8 is present, and the log line 'PATH CHOSEN ... (ticket|B8)' names the variant. The essential attribution guard is procedural: before reading any number, grep the log for the sm_90a build line, binaryVersion/ptxVersion, the canary/self-check lines and PATH CHOSEN, and confirm splitkv_verify_wgmma_kernel appears in the verify_16/32 profile (LESSONS 2026-10-25: wgmma builds have silently measured the fallback). The next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: P rounded to e4m3 for the PV wgmma: SGLang's own FA3 fp8 kernel does this, so it matches the baseline's precision and the output passed under the same bounds for FA3. Stage 2 used f16 PV, though, so rel L2 will rise above ~1.6e-3. Tighten nothing, but log the self-check error and the per-row max to see headroom against the 3%-floor bound and the 5x per-row bound (low risk).

The module-level int32[64] ticket buffer is a zero scratch buffer allocated at import, not derived from data, and reset in-kernel by the last CTA, so it is allowed. It must be per-module (not shared with full-decode-splitkv-s2-streamk-ticket's buffer if both land). The self-check's two graph replays must verify the reset.

Setting TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST in os.environ is a process-wide change. Set it only around this module's load_inline and restore it afterwards, or pass the -gencode flags via extra_cuda_cflags, so the harness's own environment and other builds are not altered (the 'edits loaded modules / harness' rule is the concern, and this keeps it clearly clean).

The import-time self-check calls torch.cuda.synchronize() and cudaFuncGetAttributes; that is fine at import, but neither may appear on the kernel_fn path. No subprocess or multiprocessing anywhere (the -inproc variant correctly removes it).

Every-key is preserved: stream-K covers every 64-token tile of every request, and only the causal mask inside the 8-token block applies. The mask must be applied on every tile overlapping [seq_b - 8, seq_b), including when that span straddles two tiles or two CTA segments (seq % 64 in 1..7 is in the self-check, which is good).

Hang risk: an mbarrier arrival-count or phase bug deadlocks instead of faulting, which costs a 15-minute timeout and gives no log. Bound every mbarrier try_wait / EMPTY wait loop (e.g. 2^24 iterations), and on overrun set the device error flag and return, so the canary detects it and falls back.
open_questions: Does the rebased stage-2 ring lay out K and V rows interleaved per token (256-B pitch) or as separate 64x128-B K and V sub-tiles? The SW128 K-major B descriptor needs the latter.

Does ptxas confirm <= 128 regs with 0 local bytes, and does cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor report 2 at ~108 KB smem? If it reports 1, the grid of 2 x SM runs in two waves and the result is not a test of the design.
How large is the in-kernel ticket merge tail (last CTA per request merges ~grid/B slots x 32 KB)? A clock64 stamp in the self-check would separate it from the main loop in the next stage.

If M2 is missed with no spills, can the next stage get per-phase clock64 timings (gather wait, QK, softmax, P permute, V transpose, PV) in the self-check, so stage 4 is not built on another inferred bottleneck?
Should the fallback be master's paired FA3 path (correct) rather than the 'unpaired FA3 path' the spec names? Confirm the implementer gates pairing on the new module's success flag.
